name: ProEnergy
ownership: private — Energy Capital Partners acquired majority interest Sep 5, 2024 (from Eos Partners / ACON Investments affiliates, equity holders since 2012; terms undisclosed). ECP describes the platform as a vertically integrated aeroderivative gas-turbine business: a development arm (the 2.4 GW WattBridge ERCOT peaker fleet, since divested), global aeroderivative services, and equipment/EPC manufacturing.
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: ProEnergy is the supply-chain arbitrage play in FEOC-immune AIDC power — it refurbishes retired Boeing 747/767 jet-engine cores (GE CF6-80C2) into its own-spec PE6000 aeroderivative package (48 MW ISO, 5-minute start, LM6000-interchangeable) and can deliver in 2027 while GE Vernova's order book is effectively sold out to 2030. The AIDC book: 21 PE6000s (>1 GW) to two unnamed data-center projects on 5-7-year bridge structures, plus 13 units (650 MW) to Crusoe for hyperscale AI factories (April 2026, delivery summer 2027). The proof-of-model is the 2.4 GW WattBridge ERCOT peaker fleet it developed, built, and then sold — CPS Energy took 1,632 MW for ~$1.387B (Sep 2025) and South Texas Electric Cooperative took 768 MW for $768M (Apr 2026), with ProEnergy retaining long-term O&M on all of it and recycling ~$2.16B into the AIDC contracted-power push. There is no BESS offering anywhere in the platform — every ProEnergy turbine campus is an open storage-attach socket, but FEOC optics steer that attach toward non-Chinese cells.
ecosystemRole: We assess ProEnergy as the mid-block (~50 MW/unit) specialist of the gas-bridge cohort squeezing containerized BESS out of AIDC energy budgets — between ERock/VoltaGrid's reciprocating fleets below and GE Vernova's heavy frames above. Its moat is not technology but access: a claimed ~1,000 CF6-80C2 retirements over the next decade supply cores no OEM queue controls, and its vertically integrated Sedalia campus (own-spec parts, string-test cells, package assembly, EPC, O&M) converts them to delivered megawatts years ahead of OEM lead times. For Hithium it is a demand-shaper and a latent channel: >1.65 GW of announced AIDC turbine capacity with zero storage attached — yet.

productsAndServices.name: PE6000 aeroderivative package (the AIDC product)
productsAndServices.description: Unveiled Nov 21, 2023 after a $115M, 7-year program: 48 MW ISO / 50.2 MW gross, 8,800 Btu/kWh gross heat rate, 5-minute start, 99% start reliability, multi-fuel, 35% hydrogen-ready, 25 ppm NOx / 59 ppm CO engine-out. Architecture: an overhauled GE CF6-80C2 high-bypass turbofan core (747-400/767/MD-11/A300 fleets) mated to newly manufactured hot-section and power-turbine parts built to ProEnergy's own spec — deliberately interchangeable with the GE LM6000 but OEM-independent, using advanced metallurgies and directed-energy-deposition additive manufacturing. Emissions kit: ammonia SCR/CO catalyst (company-claimed 90% NOx / 95% CO removal); EnergyLink Direct Injection SCR demonstrated ≤2.5 ppm NOx behind an operating unit at Braes Bayou — aimed squarely at data-center-grade permits. Water-spray injection adds up to ~20% hot-day output (water consumption undisclosed — a live issue in arid AIDC markets).
productsAndServices.positioning: Wins the ~50 MW-block segment on availability: quotes 2027 delivery vs GE Vernova LM6000 waitlists of 3-5 years and heavy-duty slots of ~10 GW open across 2029-2030 against 100 GW under contract. Competes with GE's LM2500XPRESS directly at Crusoe (which dual-sources 29 XPRESS alongside 13 PE6000s), with recips (Wärtsilä/Cat/INNIO) on footprint-per-MW and block size, and with Boom's announced 'Superpower' 42 MW entrant.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Three routes: straight equipment sale (Crusoe), turnkey EPC, or 'Contracted Power' — ProEnergy finances/owns/operates and the customer avoids capex; long-term Total Care O&M attaches in all cases
productsAndServices.targetSegments: AI data centers needing 5-7-year bridge power; utilities and co-ops needing fast dispatchable capacity; international O&M
productsAndServices.roadmap: 75 packages fabricated since 2020, 52 more in assembly or on order (Oct 2025) — a run-rate approaching ~15-25/year; Center of Excellence floor space expanding ~40%; >$1B infrastructure investment through 2028; hydrogen string-testing since 2022.

productsAndServices.name: Contracted Power / develop-build-sell IPP model
productsAndServices.description: The WattBridge playbook: develop and build LM6000-powered ERCOT peakers (six Houston-area plants, 2.4 GW, 2020-2024), then divest to utilities while retaining O&M. CPS Energy bought four plants (1,632 MW, ~$1.387B, Sep 2025); South Texas Electric Cooperative bought two (768 MW, $768M, Apr 2026). The ~$2.16B recycled, plus ECP capital, funds AIDC contracted-power deals where ProEnergy owns the bridge asset.
productsAndServices.positioning: The divest-but-keep-O&M structure converts merchant development risk into utility-grade exits plus annuity service revenue — and proves to AIDC customers that the fleet runs (the first PE6000 validated at a WattBridge site with 100+ starts).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Asset sales to munis/co-ops; 25-year PPAs (NB Power build-own-operate, 400 MW, COD 2028); O&M/Total Care contracts retained
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Municipal utilities and co-ops; provincial utilities; data-center developers wanting opex-only power
productsAndServices.roadmap: NB Power 400 MW BOO (COD 2028); UNS Electric Black Mountain AZ permit revision for 4 PE6000s (~189 MW); watch for the first named AIDC contracted-power (owned-asset) deal.

productsAndServices.name: Aeroderivative services, parts & depot (the legacy cash engine)
productsAndServices.description: Global LM6000/LM2500 field services and O&M since 2002; own-spec parts manufacturing; Houston aero depot with 120-day major overhauls (65-day case documented) and PE6000 lease engines; PowerFLX (LM6000-based optimized/recommissioned packages) and AeroAdvantage engine programs; Egypt Total Care contracts (Sharm El Sheikh, Port Said).
productsAndServices.positioning: The services base is what makes the refurb-core model credible — ProEnergy overhauls CF6-80C2 cores in-house rather than buying OEM overhauls, keeping cost and schedule internal.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct O&M and parts contracts; depot services; lease engines
productsAndServices.roadmap: Sedalia campus (90 acres / ~900,000 sq ft) expanding; Houston depot throughput compressing overhaul cycles.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess ProEnergy's core advantage as schedule arbitrage, not technology: refurbished CF6-80C2 cores plus a vertically integrated Sedalia campus deliver ~50 MW blocks in 2027 while OEM queues run to 2029-2030. That window is real but closing — GE Vernova aero output rose 32% year-over-year in Q1 2026, Boom's Superpower targets 4+ GW/yr by 2030, and recip incumbents are adding tens of GW of capacity. The company's rush to book AIDC bridges now is rational urgency.

(High confidence) Every ProEnergy AIDC campus is an open BESS-attach socket: no storage offering exists anywhere in the platform, while the industry architecture converges on turbine-plus-BESS hybrids for GPU transients, ride-through, and peak-shave. For Hithium the >1.65 GW announced book is addressable attach demand — but FEOC/§154 optics on these flagship-visibility projects push the paired storage toward non-Chinese cells; the realistic play is through the EPC/owner layer, not ProEnergy itself.

(Medium confidence) The unnamed customers behind the 21-unit, >1 GW order are the highest-value intelligence gap in the gas-bridge cohort — identifying them identifies which campuses have already committed their bridge-power budgets and, by elimination, which have not.

(Medium confidence) The develop-build-sell-keep-O&M model (WattBridge → CPS/STEC, ~$2.16B) is the financial engine to watch: ECP ownership plus recycled proceeds position ProEnergy to own AIDC bridge assets outright ('Contracted Power'), which would make it a battery buyer someday rather than merely an equipment vendor — the same evolution path VoltaGrid took.

(Low confidence) Permitting is the category's shared soft spot: 8,800 Btu/kWh simple-cycle heat rates invite opposition in non-attainment areas, EPA is reportedly tightening on long-duration 'mobile' turbine fleets, and SCR mitigations add ammonia logistics and water. A hard permitting turn would compress the bridge window and accelerate BESS-heavy alternatives — the scenario where Hithium's addressable AIDC surface re-expands fastest.

financials.commentary: Aggregator revenue figures (~$100M) are implausibly low against 900+ employees, a 2.4 GW build-out, and $2.16B of asset sales — disregard them. The real economics are unobservable until a filing or exit; the visible signals are throughput (75 built, 52 in flight) and the divestiture prices (~$850-1,000/kW for operating ERCOT peakers).
